## Session Narrative — Megatron-DeepSpeed GPT-3 Medium 350M on Tuolumne

The session ran the full dftracer pipeline (system-detect through optimizer + report) against the argonne-lcf Megatron-DeepSpeed fork, targeting GPT-3 Medium 350M on 4-node x 4-rank MI300A allocations. BERT was in-scope in the original plan but was deferred and never started this session.

Build and annotation succeeded after working through several environment issues (ROCm torch wheel resolution defaulting to CUDA, DeepSpeed op-builder ROCM_HOME auto-detection, apex ROCm build producing a Python-fallback-looking op table, torchvision ABI mismatch) — each is now a persisted lesson. Python annotation reached 202/207 functions (97.6%) across the 10 core training/data files.

Baseline collection was the hardest step: getting a genuine 16-rank distributed run (not 16 independent single-rank inits) took roughly 10 attempts, each failing for a distinct, real reason. The final successful run produced clean, non-empty traces on all 16 ranks and a 2-iteration steady-state signal.

Analysis classified the workload as compute-bound (67% training-step time), with negligible I/O (0.8%, entirely confined to iteration 1's JIT + first-touch dataset reads).

Optimization dispatched all four dimensions per policy. The compute agent ran a well-replicated study and found every lever — bf16, ZeRO-1, hipBLASLt toggling — neutral or regressive. Communication produced the session's most interesting result: a trace-derived estimate suggested ~35% from switching gloo to RCCL/nccl, but the measured effect was only +1.2% — a clear demonstration that a trace-derived estimate must be checked against a real measurement before being reported as expected impact.

A false premise was caught and corrected mid-session: an early read of DeepSpeed's op-builder table was mistakenly interpreted as evidence the ROCm apex build lacked fused HIP kernels. A direct import probe showed this was wrong — fusion was already fully applied. This correction is carried forward transparently.

The session closed with a genuinely negative-but-valuable result: the baseline is already close to optimal for this workload/scale/stack. The one clearly untested high-ceiling lever is FlashAttention, blocked on a ROCm/CK build not attempted this session.

Two process gaps are noted honestly: Pipeline Policy rule 12 (dftracer_service node-counter bracketing) was never applied to any run; and two of the report-writer's own exploratory job launches collided with the compute agent's replicate study on a shared allocation, silently killing one bf16 replicate via SIGABRT.
